title: The text discusses the complex journey of Ray Hill, a former leader in Britain's Nazi movement who became an informant for an anti-fascist magazine called Searchlight. Hill's political transformation began during his 12-year stay in South Africa, where he was involved with far-right groups and uncovered a network that sheltered European right-wing terrorists. Initially a staunch racist, Hill's views began to shift due to various experiences, including a campaign against colored families in Johannesburg. The narrative highlights the connections between apartheid South Africa and ultra-right-wing organizations in Europe, illustrating how Hill's past and his eventual disillusionment with racism shaped his life and activism.
